extracted.intended_audience: readers/practitioners of early-modern alchemy and physicians (historical and practical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Narrative and dialogic guidance on making and testing the Philosophers' Stone, practical handling of the tincture, protocols for experimental transmutation, and limits/uses of a putative universal medicine for human disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of transmutation by 'Quarta' assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Probation called Quarta: melt three or four parts of Silver with one part of Gold, hammer thin, pour Aquafortis to dissolve the Silver so that Gold 'settles to the bottome, like a black powder', then reduce to Gold in the crucible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the legitimate examen by skilful artists to demonstrate genuine transmutation. Example given: the Gold produced held up under this test and even appeared to have transmuted part of the Silver (quantified later). Perform thrice in presence of noble witnesses for confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle the tincture wrapped in yellow wax to prevent loss in fumes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the tincture is exposed during melting (especially with Lead), a 'Sympathetick Operation' in fume can carry the medicine away; wrapping the matter in yellow Wax conserves it from the fume of Lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instruction: wrap the small particle of the Stone in yellow wax (or otherwise protect it) before introducing to metal in flux; when done correctly the lead will transmute into Gold within a quarter of an hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small quantity of the Tincture can suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: A very small particle (as big as a Rape-Seed or Coriander-Seed) can be sufficient to transmute multiple grains/drams of base metal into Gold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artist's claim: the charge is not great; the matter and salt are of little price. If the operator cannot rightly handle lead (and loses matter to fumes), use a larger quantity of lead (two drams, half an ounce, etc.) so the small tincture's effect is not dissipated. Do not assume large bulk is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation performed entirely in a crucible over open fire
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Operation is, performed in a Crucible, from the beginning to the end, in an open Fire."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not perform in glassware; the whole projection/transmutation process is to be done in a crucible with strong bellows as needed. The account emphasizes crucible technique and control of heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and cost expectations for the true work
rubrics_metrics.description: The author records: 'The Whole Work may be begun, and plainly ended in no longer time, then four dayes' and 'no greater Cost is required, then the value of three Florens.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with other Philosophers' writings claiming seven or nine months. Caveat: true adepts may be sparse and writings ambiguous; claimed short time and low cost apply only with correct matter and adept knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Menstruum should be a 'Celestial Salt'
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Menstruum is a Celestial Salt, or a Salt of Celestial Virtue, by the benefit of which, Philosophers only dissolve the Terrene Metallick Body, and in dissolving, the noble Elixir of Philosophers is produced."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nature of the solvent is critical: a salt with 'celestial virtue' (qualitative description) rather than ordinary solvents; choice of menstruum is part of the essential secret of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory and colour markers of authentic Philosophic Matter and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of the Stone and process: glass-like fragments of 'the colour of pale Sulphur'; during fusion lead showed a 'most beautiful saffron-coloured Tincture', then colour like Blood when poured, and when cold 'shined with the colour of the best Gold.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sensory signs (color changes, glassy or saffron tincture, final gold sheen) are given as evidence of correct matter and successful projection; the narrative treats them as diagnostic stages to observe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead vapours corrupt metals and can produce brittle glass
rubrics_metrics.description: "For all Gold, Silver, Tin, Mercury, and like Metals, are corrupted by Lead Vapours, and likewise converted to a brittle Glass."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand interactions of vapours during fusion; shielding (wax/paper) and proper crucible technique mitigate corruption. Interpret glassy residues as evidence of vapor-induced corruption rather than genuine transmutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify transmutation effect (observationally measured yield)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed proportion: 'every Dram of Gold acquired from the Silver for an augmentation to it self, one Scruple... the five drams of Gold, attracted to it self from the Silver, five Scruples... the whole weight ... was six drams, and two Scruples, of a more vile Metal, into Gold.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeatable assays and weighings to document claimed transmutations; the narrator performed multiple trials and quantitative examinations (including mixing with Antimony) to assess loss and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate metal by skilled gold/silversmith assay and offer of market value
rubrics_metrics.description: After production, the narrator and witnesses took the metal to a skilled Silversmith who judged it 'Gold most excellent' and offered '50 Florens' per ounce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical verification includes artisan examination and market valuation as social proof of quality. Combine technical assay (Quarta) with practical appraisal by competent craftsmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's duty when universal medicine is lacking: use remedies with known effect
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is the part of a good Physician... to adhibit to the Diseases of the Sick... such Curations; or Remedies as for restoring Sanity as in which he (from the effect) certainly knows, that a virtue of healing is incited."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a putative universal elixir for all cases; instead apply simple, observed remedies whose effects are known. Practice relies on observable therapeutic virtues and tailored application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of a universal medicine for human disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The text lists many reasons it would not universally cure: differences of Age, Sex, Constitution, Stage of Disease, whether disease is inveterate or recent, and whether ferment is promoted or precipitated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical application must account for patient-specific variables (young vs old, male vs female, tender vs robust, disease chronicity). A universal cure is philosophically possible but practically constrained by human variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match remedies to humoral/part-specific signatures (example mappings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples mapping types of 'Scorbutick' venome to corrective herbs: saline acid (Peter) — volatile bitter salt of Scurvy-grass; saline bitter (Paul) — acid fixed salt of Sorrel; sweet moist (Matthias) — fixed bitter drying Sulphur of Fumitory; saline drying (Luke) — sweet moist Mercury of Brook-lime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external signs and 'signatures' to determine the specific corrective herb; do not assume one herb cures all scurvy-like conditions. This is prescriptive clinical matching based on humoral theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission from a true Adept is required to learn the Work
rubrics_metrics.description: "Out of the books of them, who triumph in the glory of Adept, no one man can learn the way of preparing, nor know their First Matter... no Lover of this Art, can find the Art... without the Communication of some true Adept Man."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writings are insufficient; experiential transmission or apprenticeship with a proven adept is presented as necessary. Practical learning, not textual study alone, is emphasized as a criterion for competence.
